checks.Title: Seduce, don't just observe
checks.Evidence: There are genuine seductive textures — the camel breathing hay-and-dust on the elevated walkway while six thousand oblivious commuters flow around it, the boy who smells of stone and fungus, the android ferryman paid in a worthless transit receipt — but these strange-beautiful moments are consistently interrupted by dense worldbuilding exposition (Consensus credentials, Halcyon routing codes, TESSERA Docents, Ferrogate subsidiaries) that reads as procedural rather than enchanting.
checks.Fix: Trim the bureaucratic/corporate exposition passages (credential systems, routing codes, subsidiary signage) and let the sensory-uncanny beats — the camel, the warm patch of ground, the slate that was already listening for her — breathe longer before the plot machinery resumes.

checks.Title: Open with the world doing its work
checks.Evidence: The opening lines do establish a grounded transactional beat (paying Φ3 at the gate, the dispatcher not looking at her) but within two paragraphs the prose pivots straight into a violent job with dialogue about 'corner position,' gray-market neuretics, and a documentation man sizing her up — the world's ordinary labor is a two-sentence backdrop before plot machinery (the deal, the bottle-strike, the flight) takes over.
checks.Fix: Extend the freight-yard opening into a longer unhurried beat of workers, cargo, and routine before introducing the deal or the violence, so the reader falls into the world's texture before being asked to follow a plot thread.

checks.Title: Gloss first mentions in-voice, never dump
checks.Evidence: Several proprietary terms get a clean in-voice gloss ('Neuretics: the mesh grown into your skull before you turn ten, meant to seal at twelve and go quiet for life') but others land as unglossed density spikes — 'TESSERA was the Consensus civic net' is a clean aside, while 'Consensus instruments logged the whole field as dead-well cold-reads' and terms like 'GLMZ ground,' 'Waxwing Neuromedia civic skins,' 'Halcyon Combine, Strategic Resources,' and 'the Thread's pods' arrive with no orientation at all, assuming the reader already knows the geography and faction map.
checks.Fix: Give each newly introduced proper noun (TESSERA, Consensus, Halcyon, the Thread, GLMZ) the same one-clause in-voice touch the neuretics and Pulse hub get, so a first-time reader isn't left inferring faction/geography meaning purely from context accumulation.

checks.Title: Never an acronym before its term
checks.Evidence: 'TESSERA was the Consensus civic net' is glossed properly, but numerous acronyms appear bare with no prior expansion at all: 'GLMZ' is used ('the first GLMZ ground she'd touched') with no expansion anywhere on the page, and 'MO-556' and 'GG-9' are given as if the reader already knows the naming convention, while 'Halcyon Combine, Strategic Resources' introduces 'OBERON' as a bare name with no expansion since it's presented as a proper name, not flagged as an acronym.
checks.Fix: Add an in-voice gloss the first time GLMZ appears (e.g., 'Any book could be a reader's first Gray-zone Liminal Metro Zone—GLMZ—book' rephrased into Sasha's narration) and similarly expand MO-556/GG-9 on first mention if they are meant to be read as acronyms rather than model numbers.

checks.Title: Give the POV character one human crack
checks.Evidence: The clearest human crack is Dawit's 'Then look at me' beat—'She didn't ask men for things'—and the moment with the man who walked back into the light, where Sasha deliberately gives him an out because she's tired of every quiet costing her a burned door. Both are genuine flashes of interiority beyond function.
checks.Fix: Trim the surrounding tradecraft-and-worldbuilding density around those two beats so the human flash lands with a clean, isolated beat instead of being immediately buried under the next action sequence or lore reveal.

checks.Title: Land one beat past the handoff
checks.Evidence: The final beat—'The doors sealed behind the cat's tail. The pod pulled into the dark.'—does land a quiet gesture (last through the door, cat at heel) rather than resolving the plot, but it's preceded by a paragraph of explicit thematic summary ('She didn't know if the packet had reached anyone... She only knew the pull in her chest hadn't stopped') that edges toward editorializing the stakes rather than trusting the image to carry them.
checks.Fix: Cut the summarizing 'She didn't know... she only knew' paragraph and end on the concrete image of stepping through last with the cat, letting the doors sealing and the pod's dark swallow the meaning without narrating it.

checks.Title: Reward re-reading without requiring it
checks.Evidence: The recurring 'ground goes blood-warm' motif, the neuretic mesh detail, and the four-second interval where 'the outside came up level with the inside' are exactly the kind of gestures that reward a second pass with hindsight meaning — but the story is so dense with unresolved lore (the man on the camel, OBERON, the boy, the wells, TESSERA, the Arrangement) that a first-time reader may struggle to get a genuinely complete story rather than a string of deferred mysteries.
checks.Fix: Tighten the ending beats so the first-pass reader receives clear closure on Sasha's immediate arc (the drill exposure, her physical wound, her choice to stay) even while the cosmic mythology remains intentionally open for rereading.

checks.Title: Elevate, don't reconstruct
checks.Evidence: The prose is dense, immersive, and largely self-sufficient (Kankakee, corner position, the Φ currency, neuretics all get sensory/functional grounding on first mention), but the back half stacks unexplained proper nouns and lore-fragments at speed — TESSERA, GLMZ, Halcyon Combine, OBERON, the Arrangement, the camel-rider, the boy in the wall, Consensus credentials, the Schism — without the same integrative context-work the opening gave 'neuretics' or 'Pulse hub,' asking a first-time reader to absorb a whole cosmology in one long unbroken sprint.
checks.Fix: Add a few brief grounding beats (a sentence of context or a character's plain reaction) at the introduction of the heaviest new-mythology nouns (TESSERA, Halcyon/OBERON, the Arrangement, the boy/android/boat sequence) so newcomers get a foothold without altering the plot or trimming the existing scenes.

checks.Title: Orient through GLMZ's five pillars
checks.Evidence: The prose weaves all five pillars into texture: neuretics are explicitly explained as failed-seal implants that stratify who can 'compete' (Sasha's unsealed mesh, governed vs ungoverned ad-filtering); nanites/infrastructure appear as Pulse maglev, cargo slugs, and credential-gated access panels shaping daily movement; CorpoNations (Halcyon, Ferrogate, Waxwing) issue credentials, own city blocks, and price a person's life like inventory ('Extraction Continuity — Priority One. Asset Recovery — Priority Two'); the Gray Zone is named repeatedly as the law-optional space fixers and hunters operate in; the Schism surfaces as literal breach wells with frequencies (19Hz dead, 72Hz live) and an entity ('the man on the camel') that treats reality's wound as a place people 'dig toward'; and AIs-as-agents appear via OBERON, a named machine officer of record ranking wells above the asset, plus the enigmatic camel-rider faction with its own agenda about closing breaches.
